title: Forty days hungry (Matthew 4:1–11)
hookLine: bread, a leap, the kingdoms of the world, three temptations and three refusals

cards: Afterwards he was hungry. That's all Matthew says about forty days and forty nights without food, after the spirit led Jesus into the desert.
Not a missed lunch: the kind of hunger where the head goes light and every thought bends toward bread. And that's exactly when the tempter comes. Not on day one, when he's strong.
At the end, when he's weakest. Three offers, one after another.

teach.b: First, bread. If you are the Son of God, the tempter says, tell these stones to become loaves. It's reasonable; he's starving.
The answer, in the Douay-Rheims: "Not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word that proceedeth from the mouth of God." Bread matters, but a person is more than a stomach. Second, a leap.

The devil takes him to the highest point of the Temple and says throw yourself down, quoting a psalm about angels catching him. Even scripture can be used as bait. Jesus answers: you shall not tempt the Lord your God.
Don't force God to prove himself. Third, everything.

teach.h: ALL THE KINGDOMS, FOR ONE BOW.
teach.b: From a very high mountain, all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, if he bows down once. The answer: "Begone, Satan: for it is written, The Lord thy God shalt thou adore, and him only shalt thou serve."
All three answers come from the book of Deuteronomy, from Moses speaking to Israel after forty years in the wilderness.

teach.h: NOT IN BREAD ALONE DOTH MAN LIVE.
teach.b: Israel was tested in the desert for forty years; Jesus for forty days, answering with Israel's own words. The Church builds a season on this story.

Lent is forty days, and on its first Sunday the Gospel is the temptation in the desert. Catholics fast and give things up then, not because comfort is bad, but to find out what they're really living on.

how: Catholics keep Lent as forty days of prayer, fasting and almsgiving; the Gospel on the First Sunday of Lent is the temptation in the desert, and many give up a comfort for the season.

games.q: you've fasted forty days. you're starving. a voice says: if you're God's Son, just turn these stones into bread. what do you say?
o: say that we don't live on bread alone.
games.why: he answers with Deuteronomy: "Not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word that proceedeth from the mouth of God."

practice: Run through the three offers once more: bread, the easy comfort; the leap, the need for proof; the kingdoms, getting your way.
Notice which one tugs hardest today, if any does, and name it without judging, the way you'd name the weather. Then ask gently what else you're hungry for, and if you pray, bring that hunger to God.

wordCard.voice: Temptation. Three offers from the tempter in the desert, each met with words from scripture.

orig.note: Greek: a testing, a trial, a temptation. The same family of words as lead us not into temptation.
